blocks.content: VOLUME marks a path inside the image as one that should be persisted outside the container's writable layer, a hint baked into the image itself about where meaningful data lives.

Declaring VOLUME /data in a Dockerfile tells Docker that this path holds data meant to outlive the container, Docker automatically creates an anonymous volume for it if one is not explicitly provided at docker run time.

blocks.alt: A path explicitly flagged as meant to persist

blocks.content: 2. It Lives Outside the Normal Writable Layer
blocks.text: 2. It Lives Outside the Normal Writable Layer

blocks.content: Data written to a path declared as a volume is stored separately from the container's ordinary writable layer, which is exactly why it survives removing the container, while everything else in that writable layer does not. The full mechanics, named volumes, bind mounts, and the difference between them, are covered in the dedicated Docker Volumes module.

blocks.alt: Volume data lives apart from the disposable writable layer

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: VOLUME marks a path as meant to persist beyond the container's own lifecycle, not just live in its disposable writable layer.
The full volumes system (named volumes, bind mounts, and how they differ) is covered in depth in the Docker Volumes module.
